species.name: Atlantic Sharpnose Shark
species.quote: Atlantic Sharpnose | | 1 per person per day | |
species.limit: 1 per person per day
species.notes: Federal Highly Migratory Species Permit with a Shark Endorsement are required in federal waters to recreationally fish for, retain, possess, or land sharks. All sharks must be landed with fins, head and tail naturally attached. Recreational anglers may only catch sharks using a rod & reel or handline. All other gears prohibited. Additionally, angers fishing recreationally for sharks are required to use non-offset, non-stainless steel circle hooks, except when fishing with flies or artificial lures.
userNotes: Rod & reel or handline only; non-offset, non-stainless circle hooks required with natural bait.
Land with fins, head and tail naturally attached.
In federal waters (beyond 3 mi) you need a federal HMS Angling permit with a shark endorsement.
Gigging sharks is unlawful; sharks may not be taken by gill net.

species.name: Blue Catfish
species.quote: The daily bag limit for blue catfish harvest is 150 fish per day per person on all state waterways except the daily bag limit remains 25 fish per day for Lake Marion, Lake Moultrie, the section of the Pee Dee River from the state border with North Carolina south to the Highway 301 bridge, and the upper reach of the Santee River. It is also unlawful to possess more than two blue catfish greater than thirty-two inches in length in any one day in Lake Marion, Lake Moultrie, the upper reach of the Santee River, the section of the Pee Dee River from the state border with North Carolina south to the Highway 301 bridge, and the Congaree and Wateree rivers.

Exception: 25/day for Lake Marion, Lake Moultrie, the Pee Dee River (NC border to Hwy 301 bridge), and the upper Santee River. No more than 2 blue catfish over 32 inches per day in Lake Marion, Lake Moultrie, upper Santee River, the Pee Dee exception area, and the Congaree and Wateree rivers." Freshwater limits page lists Blue Catfish as "See limits in Freshwater Nongame Fishing Regulations section."
